prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Looking back, one sports historian argued that the rule of 1868 had ______ the game.

worlds.passage: In 1868 the twenty-four football clubs of a northern county's league, from its towns and villages alike, adopted a new rule for their matches. Before it, a scrum could hold forty players kicking at each other's shins. The rule ended a scrum once the ball was held and barred any kick that missed the ball. Local papers, which had listed dozens of broken legs each season, listed four in 1870. Old players complained that a man could get through a season without a bruise worth showing, and kept turning out for their clubs each week. Looking back, one sports historian argued that the rule of 1868 had ______ the game.
worlds.explanation: The rule ended long scrums and banned kicks at players, broken legs fell from dozens to four, and veterans complained of a season without bruises; combining these shows the rule made the game far less violent, so it "tamed" the game. "Unbalanced" fails because the rule limited rough play for every side alike. "Splintered" fails because the old players kept playing for their clubs under the rule. "Urbanized" fails because the rule changed how the game was played, not where or by whom.

unbalanced.quote: barred any kick that missed the ball
unbalanced.why: the rule limited violence for every side equally; nothing in it favors one kind of club

splintered.quote: kept turning out for their clubs
splintered.why: even the players who disliked the rule kept playing under it, so the game did not divide

urbanized.quote: turning out for their clubs each week
urbanized.why: the same clubs went on playing as before, so the game did not move to the towns

worlds.passage: In 1868 the twenty-four football clubs of a northern county's league, from its towns and villages alike, adopted a new rule for their matches. It let a side that caught the ball keep it for as long as its forwards could hold off a tackle. Clubs from the colliery villages, whose forwards were the heaviest men in the county, won fifty-one of their next sixty matches. A title that had changed hands nearly every year went to one of three colliery clubs in each of the next twelve seasons. Looking back, one sports historian argued that the rule of 1868 had ______ the game.
worlds.explanation: The rule rewarded sheer weight in the forwards, so the colliery clubs, with the heaviest men, began winning almost every match and every title: the rule "unbalanced" the game. "Tamed" fails because the rule did nothing to make play less rough; it made strength decisive. "Splintered" fails because the clubs stayed in one league competing for one title. "Urbanized" fails because the clubs that rose were village clubs that already belonged to the league.

tamed.quote: as long as its forwards could hold off a tackle
tamed.why: the rule made physical strength count for more, the opposite of reining in rough play

splintered.quote: went to one of three colliery clubs
splintered.why: there was still a single title in a single league

urbanized.why: the winners were village clubs, so the game did not shift to the towns

worlds.passage: In 1868 the twenty-four football clubs of a northern county's league, from its towns and villages alike, adopted a new rule for their matches. It forbade carrying the ball in the hands. Eleven of the clubs refused to play under it and left the league, and the next year they drew up a rulebook of their own that kept the old handling game. By 1880 the county papers printed two league tables each week, and no club appeared in both. Looking back, one sports historian argued that the rule of 1868 had ______ the game.
worlds.explanation: The rule drove eleven clubs out, they wrote rules of their own preserving the handling game, and the county ended up with two separate tables; combining these shows the rule broke the game into rival forms, so it "splintered" the game. "Tamed" fails because the rule's effect was division, not less rough play. "Unbalanced" fails because the two groups stopped competing against each other, so neither was favored. "Urbanized" fails because the same clubs went on playing where they always had, in two codes.

tamed.why: the outcome of the rule was a split over handling, not a gentler game

unbalanced.why: the two groups no longer played each other, so neither was given an edge

urbanized.why: the existing clubs simply divided; nothing moved the game into towns

worlds.passage: In 1868 the twenty-four football clubs of a northern county's league, from its towns and villages alike, adopted a new rule for their matches. It required every match to be played on an enclosed ground with marked boundaries and a gate, and the league paid every club's rent from gate money. The village clubs, which had played across open common land, moved to fenced grounds in the nearest mill or market town and took the town's name. By 1875 every match in the league was played in a town. Looking back, one sports historian argued that the rule of 1868 had ______ the game.
worlds.explanation: The rule required fenced grounds that only towns had, the league covered the rent, and the village clubs moved into the towns, so that by 1875 every match was a town match: the rule "urbanized" the game. "Tamed" fails because the rule governed grounds, not how roughly the game was played. "Unbalanced" fails because the league paid every club's rent, so the move cost no club an advantage. "Splintered" fails because the village clubs stayed in the league rather than forming a rival game.

tamed.why: the rule set conditions for the ground, not limits on play

unbalanced.quote: paid every club's rent from gate money
unbalanced.why: the cost of the new grounds was shared, so no club was handicapped by the rule

splintered.why: all the clubs, village ones included, stayed in one league
